links.comparator_used: Single-assay models trained on one assay's data (tested for cross-assay generalization)
links.effect: Pooled multi-assay training improved cross-assay robustness compared with single-assay models; no numeric effect for this comparison in the abstract. Separately, models applied across platforms without recalibration had MAE 2.62, versus 0.0419 for XGBoost within-platform.
links.tradeoff: Pooling did not remove platform dependence: direct cross-platform application without recalibration caused a substantial performance decline.
links.quote: Extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) achieved the most accurate and stable predictions under data-sufficient, within-platform conditions with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.0419, while pooled multi-assay training improved cross-assay robustness compared with single-assay models.
